# 1 Maccabees Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_001_page_001.jpg

---

1. This is what happened after Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian king who came out of the land of Kittim — after he had crushed Darius king of Persia and Media and taken his throne, having already conquered Greece:
2. he fought war after war, seized strongholds, and cut down kings.
3. He marched to the ends of the earth, looting nations in his wake. The world went silent before him. His pride swelled without limit.
4. He built an army of overwhelming force, subjugated provinces and nations and princes, and made them all pay tribute.
5. Then he took to his bed and knew he was dying.
6. He summoned his commanders — the men who had grown up at his side — and while he still had breath, he divided his empire among them.
7. Alexander had reigned twelve years when he died.
8. His commanders each seized control of his own territory.
9. After his death they all crowned themselves kings, and their sons after them through many years. They multiplied evil across the earth.
10. Out of this rot there came a sinful offshoot: Antiochus, called Epiphanes, son of King Antiochus, who had once been a hostage in Rome. He seized the throne in the one hundred and thirty-seventh year of the Greek kingdom.
11. In those days certain lawless men rose up in Israel and misled many, saying: "Let us go make terms with the nations around us. We have been separate from them, and nothing but trouble has found us."
12. The argument seemed persuasive.
13. Some of the people ran eagerly to the king and he granted them license to live like the Gentiles.
14. They built a gymnasium in Jerusalem, in the Gentile style,
15. reversed their circumcisions, abandoned the holy covenant, sold themselves to do evil, and melted into the nations.
16. When his grip on the kingdom was secure, Antiochus set his sights on Egypt, determined to rule two kingdoms at once.
17. He swept into Egypt with massive force — chariots, war elephants, cavalry, and a fleet of warships —
18. and launched his assault on Ptolemy king of Egypt. Ptolemy broke and ran. The dead and wounded lay everywhere.
19. The fortified cities of Egypt fell. Antiochus looted the land.
20. He turned back from Egypt in the one hundred and forty-third year and marched on Israel and Jerusalem with a war machine.
21. He walked into the sanctuary with contemptuous arrogance and stripped it bare — the golden altar, the lampstand with all its fittings,
22. the table of the bread of the Presence, the libation vessels, the cups, the golden censers, the curtain, the crowns, the golden ornamentation from the face of the temple — all of it.
23. He took the silver, the gold, the sacred vessels, and every hidden treasure he could find.
24. He took everything and left for his own land, leaving massacre in his wake, speaking with monstrous arrogance.
25. And the grief that spread through Israel was overwhelming — in every corner of the land.
26. Rulers and elders moaned in anguish. Virgins and young men collapsed. The faces of the women changed color.
27. Every bridegroom lifted up a lament. She who sat in the bridal chamber wept.
28. The land shook with the grief of its people. Every family of Jacob wore shame like a garment.
29. Two years later the king dispatched a senior tax official to the cities of Judah. He arrived in Jerusalem with an imposing force.
30. He spoke to the people in friendly terms — a lie they believed. Then without warning he fell on the city like a hammer blow, killing many Israelites.
31. He looted the city and put it to the torch, tearing down its houses and the walls all around it.
32. Women and children were taken captive. Livestock was seized.
33. Then they fortified the city of David with a massive wall and strong towers, turning it into their stronghold.
34. They filled it with a foreign garrison — lawless men who dug in.
35. They stored weapons and supplies there, stacking up the plunder taken from Jerusalem. It became a trap set in the heart of the city.
36. It crouched there as a constant ambush against the sanctuary — a festering wound in Israel's side.
37. They spilled innocent blood on every side of the sanctuary. They defiled the holy place.
38. Because of them Jerusalem's people fled. The city became a dwelling place for strangers. It became alien to the children born in it, and they abandoned her.
39. Her sanctuary lay waste as a desert. Her festivals became funerals. Her sabbaths turned to mockery. Her dignity was dragged through the dirt.
40. The greater her former glory, the deeper her humiliation. Her exaltation was swallowed by grief.
41. The king issued a proclamation to his entire empire: all peoples must become one people,
42. each one abandoning his ancestral customs.
43. Every nation fell in line with his decree. Many in Israel also went along — sacrificing to idols and desecrating the sabbath.
44. He sent written orders by couriers to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah: they were to adopt customs that were foreign to the land.
45. Burnt offerings, sacrifices, drink offerings in the sanctuary — prohibited. Sabbaths and feast days — profaned.
46. The sanctuary and the holy people — defiled.
47. Pagan altars, sacred groves, idol shrines — to be built. Pigs and unclean animals — to be sacrificed.
48. Sons — to be left uncircumcised. Souls — to be polluted with every manner of uncleanness.
49. The Torah — to be forgotten. Every ordinance — to be overturned.
50. Anyone who disobeyed would die.
51. He wrote these orders across his entire kingdom and appointed enforcers over the people. He commanded the cities of Judah to sacrifice, one town at a time.
52. Many from the people rallied to them — everyone who had abandoned the Torah — and they brought evil down on the land.
53. They drove Israel into hiding wherever a hiding place could be found.
54. On the fifteenth day of Chislev, in the one hundred and forty-fifth year, they set up the desolating abomination on the altar of burnt offerings, and throughout the cities of Judah they erected pagan altars in every direction.
55. At the doors of houses and in the streets they burned pagan incense.
56. Wherever they found Torah scrolls they tore them apart and burned them.
57. If any man was found with a scroll of the covenant, if anyone held fast to the Torah, the king's decree meant death.
58. Month after month they came down on Israelites found in the cities with brutal force.
59. On the twenty-fifth day of the month they sacrificed on the profane altar built over the altar of burnt offerings.
60. Under the decree, women who had circumcised their sons were executed —
61. their dead infants tied around their necks. Those who had performed the circumcisions were killed too, along with the whole family.
62. But many in Israel held firm. They steeled themselves and refused to eat unclean food.
63. They chose death over defilement, death over profaning the holy covenant. And they died.
64. Terrible wrath came crashing down upon Israel.
